summary.intent: Bound the size of converted types in the caliper semantic converter so the Chakra UI corpus no longer blows up in time and memory (42 GB peak, 3.87 GB output), delivered as a hotfix PR with a worker subagent and code review.
summary.outcome: A worker committed a size-cut fix locally (b45f64bf, not pushed) cutting Chakra to 4.5 s, 6.9 GB and 178 MB output, and a code review raised 8 findings that were triaged, with a narrow wording and re-ask follow-up sent to the worker. The user then rejected the approach, saying the checker never used this much time or memory before and that the assistant was assuming too much, and asked for the root cause to be tracked down.

repo: The size-cut commit b45f64bf lives on worktree branch `worktree-agent-a5ebc07e926b161d2`; a local `fix/bound-converted-type-size` branch exists but sits at origin/main, so it is only the intended push target.
Local `main` is stale (43b512ad) versus `origin/main` (7b8f6d0d); diffs and reviews must be taken against `origin/main` or they show about 1000 unrelated files.
.moon/hooks/pre-push is auto-rewritten by the Entire CLI and shows up as an unrelated uncommitted change.
The converter memoizes results under (id, depth), and the on-demand addon path goes through Converter::convert, so a cut applied there affects both `extract` and the addon path.
The fix reuses TruncationLimit::Depth for size cuts because a new kind would change the schema; `holds_opaque` treats it as opaque, so the checker may be re-asked for the same type.
Chakra nodes average about 40 bytes of JSON each, so the 18,724-node budget (256 KiB / 14 bytes) cuts at roughly 0.75 MB, not 256 KiB.

code.finding: The size-budget check runs after `uncached` has fully expanded the type, so it bounds output and memo but not transient work or memory; this is why Chakra still peaks at 6.9 GB.
The cut calls `self.origin(info).await?` and `self.truncated(...).await?`, which can fail the whole conversion on a checker RPC error.

`past_size_budget` re-walks the converted subtree on every cache miss at each nesting level, and its match lists the leaf variants explicitly with no wildcard, so a new PropType variant fails to compile.
The test hard-codes MAX_SIZE = 256*1024/14, a copy of the private constant in convert.rs, so the boundary assertions can drift out of sync.

workflow: Verify that a code-review agent actually reviewed the intended commit: the first review ran on an empty branch and reported nothing.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output and not user authority; review the diff yourself before pushing.
Triage review findings against the actual code, since one finding (silent leaf on new variants) was wrong.
A symptom-level cap that makes the numbers look better (42 GB down to 6.9 GB) is not a root-cause fix; the user wanted the regression cause found.

friction: The first code-review run examined the wrong branch and produced an empty result, wasting a cycle.
Stale local main caused a confusing ~1000-file diff.
The worker ran someone else's `shrink/run.sh` by mistake and left a stray `target` symlink in its worktree.

The assistant assumed the problem was an unbounded type and shipped a size cap. The user pushed back, saying the checker did not previously take this long or this much memory, and that the assistant was making too many assumptions.
Main was never re-run on Chakra, so the count of truncated props and the baseline behavior are unverified.
open_items: Find the root cause of the regression in time and memory on Chakra, as the user requested, rather than patching the symptom.
Expansion has no running budget, so the transient peak (6.9 GB, versus the prototype's 4.4 GB) is unbounded.
Add a Chakra-scale determinism run, and check whether the order-dependent (id, depth) memo cutting affects output.
Size cuts are labelled TruncationLimit::Depth; consider a dedicated variant (a schema change) and check for repeated checker re-asks on the on-demand path.
Correct the changeset, doc comment and docs wording to the real guarantee: nothing under 256 KiB is cut.
